notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: White bollard with a red band that wraps all the way round; a red reflector on the front and a white one on the back.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: A thinner, curved version of the same red-banded bollard also appears.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Thin concrete poles with see-through holes ("holey poles"); the holes usually stop before the bottom.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Poles are sometimes doubled up or set as an A-frame; round concrete poles also occur.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Long white plates with the blue EU strip on the left; newer electric cars have green plates.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: All road lines are white, and a double white centre line is common and a strong hint.

notes.subject: guardrail
notes.text: Square B-type guardrails with round red reflectors, rare elsewhere in Europe.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Warning triangles have a yellow background and a thin red border; unique in Europe.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: The pedestrian crossing sign shows one horizontal line instead of zebra stripes.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Direction signs are green with a distinctive font; expressway signs are blue.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Chevrons are white with red arrows.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Letters Ł, Ń and Ż exist only in this language; Ą and Ę also appear in Lithuanian. Lots of W, and no V.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Mostly flat, green farmland with tree-lined roads; mountains only near the southern border.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Neat grey or light-red tiled sidewalks, pastel stucco houses, and roadside Catholic shrines.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Place names ending -owo are mostly in the north; -ów mostly in the south.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Landline numbers have 9 digits and the first 2 are a geographic area code.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Traditional wooden houses are common in the east, mainly Podlaskie.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Yellow pole markings are mostly in western and southern Poland.
